prompt: The code always prints 'not equal' even when x is 5. Why?
choices: "5" is not a valid String in Java
== compares object references for Strings — two String objects may not share the same reference
The if condition needs parentheses around the String
String comparison requires a semicolon after the condition
explanation: For String content comparison, use equals(): if (x.equals("5")). == checks if both variables point to the same object in memory, which may or may not be true depending on whether the JVM interns the string.
